summary: Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Peking University, he was a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti.

Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Allahabad (around 1940–1948) and held posts at Aligarh Muslim University (around 1953–1961) and the University of Rajasthan (around 1961–1970).

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College, and University of Calcutta under Sarat Chandra Das, later serving as Principal of Sanskrit College and Joint Philological Secretary of The Asiatic Society.

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indologist, philosopher, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (around 1948–1956) and as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara in 1955.

Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, with posts attested in 1999 and 2026.
Satkari Sharma Vangiya is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya, Ramachandra Jha, and Ramachandra Sastri.

Satoru Harada (born 1947) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo and held positions at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), the Eastern Institute (attested 1982), and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).
Satoru Noriyama studied Buddhist studies under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).
Satoshi Fujiwara is a Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Satoshi Hayashima works in the field of Buddhist studies. He was a research student at Ryukoku University around 2013–2014 and later served as a lecturer there from 2015 to 2017.

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, lecturing at Bukkyo University (~1993–2002) before becoming a Professor and later President (2014) at Kyoto Bunkyo University.
Satoshi Ito (born 1961) is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1990) and became a professor at Ibaraki University around 2004.
Satoshi Kono (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki is a scholar of archaeology, history, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from Kyoto University, where he also served as an Assistant Professor (attested 2016–2020).
Satya Narayan Goenka (1924–2013) was a teacher in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin from around 1955 to 1971 and founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

Satya Swarup Misra (born 1935) is an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Lucknow (attested 1958) and as Professor of Indology and Linguistics at Banaras Hindu University.

Satya Vrat Shastri (1930–2021) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of the Punjab and Banaras Hindu University. He served as Department Head and Dean at the University of Delhi and Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya.

Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) studied at Presidency University and the University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Calcutta and the University of Dhaka, and served as Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Saubhagya Pradhananga works in history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2018, she was attested as Chief of the National Archives of Nepal and as an editorial board member for the Documenta Nepalica Book Series.

Sayadaw U Pandita (1921–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw. He served as a meditation teacher at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha, succeeding Mahasi Sayadaw (1982–1991), and founded Panditarama Meditation Center, serving as abbot.
